chunks: What was narrated by ʿAlī ibn Mahziyār, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Yasār, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jundab, from Muʿāwiyah ibn Wahb, who said:
Abū ʿAbd Allāh said: The month about which it is said that it does not diminish is Dhū al-Qaʿdah, while there is no month among the months of the year that is more subject to diminution than it.

As for the statement that the year is three hundred and fifty-four days because the heavens and the earth were created in six days, which were reduced from three hundred and sixty days, this does not establish that any particular month among them must always be thirty days. Rather, it implies that the six days are distributed throughout all the months without specification or designation of which among them is deficient, such that one that may happen to be complete would be so instead of being deficient.

As for the statement that the months of the year differ in completeness and deficiency, such that among them there is a complete month and a deficient month, this also does not necessitate the opponent’s claim regarding the month of Ramaḍān as he alleged, nor regarding Shaʿbān what he ruled of its deficiency in every case. For they may indeed be as described in terms of completeness and deficiency, but they are not so according to a fixed sequence and order.

Rather, it is not to be denied that within them two consecutive months may both be complete, and two successive months may both be deficient, and even three months as we have described. And along with what we have mentioned, this still accords with the statement that among them there is a deficient month and a complete month, since explicit wording of that does not require either continuity or separation.

key_terms.التَّرْتِيبِ وَالنِّظَامِ: Fixed sequence and order; denied here as governing complete and deficient months
key_terms.التَّمَامِ: Completeness; referring to a full thirty-day month
key_terms.ثَلَاثُمِائَةٍ وَأَرْبَعَةٌ وَخَمْسُونَ: Three hundred and fifty-four days; the stated total length of the lunar year
key_terms.ذُو الْقَعْدَةِ: The month of Dhū al-Qaʿdah, mentioned here in relation to claims about month length
key_terms.شَعْبَانَ: The month of Shaʿbān, also discussed regarding deficiency
key_terms.شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ: The month of Ramaḍān, central to the disputed claim in the report
key_terms.شُهُورِ السَّنَةِ: The months of the year, discussed as varying in length
key_terms.نُقْصَانًا: Deficiency; referring to a month being less than thirty days

ai.seo_question: Can Ramaḍān or any lunar month be assumed to be always complete or deficient?
ai.summary: This report discusses the variation of lunar months in being complete or deficient and rejects the claim that a specific month is always fixed at thirty days or always deficient. It argues that completeness and deficiency occur across the months without an invariable sequence, which has implications for determining months such as Ramaḍān and Shaʿbān.
